description: Perform the exhaustive end-to-end QA audit of the Budget Tracker app and produce the full report at repo root QA_AUDIT_REPORT.md. Combine live testing (dev server + browser automation for everything that can run without Supabase/Gemini credentials) with rigorous code-level review (for everything gated behind missing credentials). The report must contain all 9 numbered deliverable sections and clearly state which branch/commit was audited and which items are Blocked due to missing external credentials. Depends on FEAT-001 (environment + baseline).
steps: Read .agents/tasks/task-qa-audit-budget-tracker/context.json and baseline-notes.md first for environment facts, missing-credential constraints, and the file map. State the audited branch (feature/budget-tracker) and commit (d563b5edd90ab59e8c092bc456c64306110de97b) at the top of the report.
Start the dev server in the background via `bash -lc 'cd /projects/sandbox/kiro-web-playground && npm run dev'` (run_in_background). Confirm the port (default 3000).

Use a browser-automation power for live testing. Activate it first via the kiro_powers tool: call action=activate for powerName 'playwright' (MCP server) OR 'agent-browser'. Prefer playwright MCP. Drive: the landing page (/), /login, /signup. For each, capture a screenshot, inspect the browser console for JS errors/warnings, inspect the network tab for failed requests (note Supabase calls will fail with placeholder/undefined env), and test at three viewports: mobile (~375px), tablet (~768px), desktop (~1280px). Save screenshots as artifacts and reference their paths in the report's 'Screenshot reference' fields.

Test client-side form validation on /login and /signup live: submit empty fields, invalid email formats, password under 6 chars (signup minLength=6), extremely long strings, special characters, SQL-injection-style strings (e.g. ' OR 1=1 --), and XSS payloads (e.g. <script>alert(1)</script>) in text inputs. Record which inputs have HTML5 validation vs. none, and whether any value is reflected unsanitized. Note the signup 2-step flow (step 1 credentials -> step 2 profile) and that pressing Enter/submit on step 1 only advances step.

Verify routing and redirects live where possible: navigate directly to /dashboard, /transactions, /budgets, /settings, /scan without a session and confirm middleware redirects to /login (or document the actual behavior when Supabase env is missing, e.g. server error). Navigate to a non-existent route and record the 404 behavior. Test browser back/forward across landing<->login<->signup.

For all Supabase/Gemini-gated behavior that cannot be exercised without credentials (actual login, signup persistence, dashboard charts with data, transactions CRUD, budgets CRUD, settings save, category CRUD, delete account, receipt OCR + AI parse), perform a thorough CODE-LEVEL review against the files in context.relevant_files and record findings as concrete bugs/risks with file+line references. Mark end-to-end functional verification of these as 'Blocked (missing credentials)' in the QA Summary, but still report the code-level issues you can prove by reading the code.

Ground findings in specific code issues actually present. Investigate and, where valid, report at least these observed issues (verify each against the source before including): (a) app/(app)/scan/page.tsx uses a raw for the receipt preview (next/image lint warning + perf) and its alt text; (b) transactions CSV export in transactions/page.tsx builds CSV by string concatenation with no escaping of commas/quotes/newlines in note or category name -> CSV injection / broken columns, and no formula-injection guard (leading =,+,-,@); (c) dashboard/transactions/budgets/settings each call an async loadData in useEffect(..., []) with no cleanup and no error/empty handling if the query errors (only checks res.data truthiness) -> silent failure states, and potential act/exhaustive-deps lint; (d) no loading/disabled guard against double-submit on the new-transaction and add-budget and add-category forms beyond the loading flag (double-click race before state flips); (e) parse-receipt route does JSON.parse on model output inside try/catch (ok) but returns 500 vs 502 inconsistently and trusts item.price/category with no whitelist enforcement of the 10 allowed categories on the server; (f) settings deleteAccount only deletes the profile row and signs out (relies on DB cascade) but does not delete the auth user, and there is no server-side reauth; (g) client-side amount validation min=0.01 but no max and parseFloat(amount) could be NaN if bypassed; (h) middleware matcher excludes image extensions and the protectedPaths use startsWith so a path like /dashboardx would also match -> over-broad protection; (i) money handled as JS floating point Number (formatCurrency uses toFixed) -> rounding risk; (j) getMonthKey/date handling uses local timezone which can shift month boundaries; (k) accessibility: mobile menu toggle button has no aria-label/aria-expanded, icon-only Trash2/close buttons lack accessible names (only some have title), Recharts/OCR have no reduced-motion consideration, color-only status indicators on budget bars.

Accessibility review (live + code): keyboard-only navigation and tab order on landing/login/signup, visible focus indicators (focus:ring-2 present on inputs but icon buttons lack it), alt text on images/icons (lucide icons are decorative SVGs without aria-hidden), ARIA labels on icon-only buttons and the mobile hamburger, color contrast of muted-foreground text and colored amounts against backgrounds (check against WCAG AA), and semantic HTML usage (verify against the steering rule; note where <div> is used for interactive or structural regions).

Performance review (live + code): observe landing page load and console performance warnings; note Tesseract.js bundle weight and that OCR runs on the main thread client-side (large receipts freeze UI), Recharts bundle size, the raw receipt preview not optimized, potential layout shifts from charts/async data, and duplicate/again-on-refresh data fetches. Record Largest observed issues.

Security review (live + code): protected-route enforcement (middleware), that anon Supabase key is public by design but RLS in supabase/schema.sql is the real guard (confirm RLS policies exist for all four tables), password masking (type=password present), token/session handling via Supabase cookies, sensitive data exposure (error.message surfaced directly to users on login/signup/insert -> possible info leak), input sanitization / XSS (React escapes by default; flag the CSV injection and any dangerouslySetInnerHTML - confirm none), the parse-receipt endpoint being unauthenticated (no user check) so anyone can spend the Gemini quota (DoS/cost risk), and OAuth callback redirect handling (open-redirect check on the `next` param in app/auth/callback/route.ts).

Write QA_AUDIT_REPORT.md at repo root with ALL of these sections in order: (1) QA Summary with audited branch+commit, total pages tested, total tests executed, passed, failed, blocked; (2) Bug Report Table with columns | ID | Severity | Priority | Component | Description |; (3) Detailed Bug Reports each with Title, Description, Steps to reproduce, Expected result, Actual result, Suggested fix, Screenshot reference; (4) UX Improvement Suggestions; (5) Security Findings; (6) Accessibility Findings; (7) Performance Findings; (8) Production Readiness Score 0-100 with justification; (9) Final Recommendation (one of: Ready for Production / Ready with Minor Fixes / Needs Major Fixes / Do Not Release). Use Severity {Critical,High,Medium,Low} and Priority {P0,P1,P2,P3} for every bug. Every suggested fix must respect the steering rule (responsive Tailwind + semantic HTML).

Ensure the report explicitly lists Blocked items (login/signup persistence, all authenticated CRUD, dashboard data, receipt scan AI/OCR) with the reason 'requires Supabase/Gemini credentials not present in the environment', so blocked is not conflated with passed or failed.
acceptance_criteria: QA_AUDIT_REPORT.md exists at the repository root and contains all 9 numbered deliverable sections in order.
The report states the audited branch (feature/budget-tracker) and commit d563b5edd90ab59e8c092bc456c64306110de97b.
The QA Summary reports total pages tested, tests executed, passed, failed, and blocked counts, and the blocked items name the missing-credential reason.
The Bug Report Table uses the exact columns | ID | Severity | Priority | Component | Description | and every row has a Severity from {Critical,High,Medium,Low} and Priority from {P0,P1,P2,P3}.
Each detailed bug report includes Title, Description, Steps to reproduce, Expected result, Actual result, Suggested fix, and a Screenshot reference field (path or 'N/A - blocked/code-level').

Findings are grounded in the actual source (reference real files/lines), not generic boilerplate; at minimum the CSV-injection, raw /next-image, unauthenticated parse-receipt endpoint, icon-button accessibility, and error-message-exposure issues are covered if verified present.
Section 8 gives a numeric 0-100 score with justification and Section 9 gives exactly one of the four allowed recommendations.
Live-tested pages (landing, login, signup) have real observations (console/network/responsive) and referenced screenshots where captured.
verification: grep -c '^#' QA_AUDIT_REPORT.md confirms the 9 sections are present (headings)
grep -E 'feature/budget-tracker|d563b5e' QA_AUDIT_REPORT.md finds the audited branch/commit reference
grep -E 'Blocked|blocked' QA_AUDIT_REPORT.md finds the blocked-items accounting
grep -E 'Ready for Production|Ready with Minor Fixes|Needs Major Fixes|Do Not Release' QA_AUDIT_REPORT.md finds the final recommendation
findings: QA_AUDIT_REPORT.md written at repo root with all 9 numbered deliverable sections, audited branch feature/budget-tracker + commit d563b5edd90ab59e8c092bc456c64306110de97b stated up top, and a Bug Report Table using the exact | ID | Severity | Priority | Component | Description | columns. 16 grounded bugs (BUG-001..BUG-016) each with Severity {Critical,High,Medium,Low} and Priority {P0,P1,P2,P3}. Final recommendation: Needs Major Fixes. Production readiness score 34/100. No em dashes in the report. LIVE TESTING: dev server started via `next dev` on port 3000 in two passes. (1) No-creds pass: EVERY route returns HTTP 500 (confirmed for / /login /signup /dashboard /transactions /budgets /settings /scan and unknown routes) with server error `Your project's URL and Key are required to create a Supabase client!` at lib/supabase/middleware.ts:9 -> middleware.ts:5. (2) Fake-but-valid-format creds pass (clearly labeled, not a functional pass): / /login /signup render 200 with expected content; /dashboard /transactions /budgets /settings /scan correctly 307-redirect to /login (auth gating logic proven correct once the Supabase client can be built); unknown route returns 404. Screenshots could NOT be persisted: the sandbox reaps background processes when each execute_bash returns, so the separate Playwright MCP browser process cannot attach to a live local server. Live evidence captured instead as HTTP status codes, rendered HTML content, and server stack traces within single-invocation runs; screenshot fields read 'N/A - ...' accordingly. CODE-REVIEW FINDINGS (all verified against source): BUG-001 Critical all-routes-500 middleware crash + missing .env.example; BUG-002 CSV injection (transactions/page.tsx exportCSV, no escaping/formula-guard); BUG-003 unauthenticated /api/parse-receipt (Gemini cost/DoS, no category whitelist server-side); BUG-004 deleteAccount only deletes profile row + signOut, never deletes auth user, no reauth; BUG-005 raw error.message surfaced to users; BUG-006 useEffect(loadData,[]) swallows errors, no empty/error states; BUG-007 double-submit races; BUG-008 raw in scan/page.tsx:234 (lint-confirmed @next/next/no-img-element); BUG-009 npm audit 7 vulns (6 high incl Next.js middleware-bypass/cache-poisoning/CSP-nonce XSS/image DoS/SSRF); BUG-010 floating-point money (toFixed); BUG-011 over-broad startsWith path matching; BUG-012 icon-only buttons + mobile hamburger lack aria-label/aria-expanded, decorative SVGs not aria-hidden; BUG-013 timezone-sensitive getMonthKey/date parsing; BUG-014 deprecated middleware->proxy convention warning; BUG-015 OAuth `next` param not allow-listed; BUG-016 amount parseFloat no max/NaN guard. Positives verified: build compiles 0 type errors, lint 0 errors/1 warning, RLS present for all 4 tables, password masking, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, semantic HTML + responsive Tailwind throughout. BLOCKED (requires Supabase/Gemini credentials not present): real login, Google OAuth callback, signup persistence, dashboard data+charts, transactions CRUD, add-transaction, budgets CRUD, settings profile/category CRUD, delete-account teardown, receipt OCR+AI end-to-end. Listed explicitly in the QA Summary as blocked (not passed/failed). No application source modified (git diff --stat empty). Only QA_AUDIT_REPORT.md and task-state files added.
